- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment swings from positive to negative (e.g., 0.80 → 0.27), model overreacts; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in following 7–14 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon; if forecast is >10% above 18-day moving average, adjust downward by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- In low-sentiment periods, model underestimates downward moves; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for 3–7 day horizon to account for volatility.
- Forecast horizon >14 days shows persistent lag; if true outcome is below 70, model often misses it; apply 1–2% correction downward for 15+ day forecasts.
